The 2026 season was Kolkata Knight Riders' nineteenth appearance in the Indian Premier League (IPL). They were one of the ten cricket teams that competed in the 2026 IPL. The team was captained by Ajinkya Rahane and coached by Abhishek Nayar.

Kolkata Knight Riders were one of the last teams to be eliminated from the 2026 IPL and finished the season in seventh place with six wins from 14 matches. Angkrish Raghuvanshi scored the most runs (422) while Kartik Tyagi took the most wickets (18) for Kolkata in the 2026 season.

Pre-season

[edit | edit source]
Further information: List of 2026 Indian Premier League personnel changes

The 2026 Indian Premier League was the 19th edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), a professional Twenty20 (T20) cricket league held in India, organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).[5] Kolkata Knight Riders had won the IPL title three times.[6] The team finished in eighth place in the previous season.[7] The tournament featured ten teams competing in 74 matches from 28 March to 31 May 2026.[8][9][10] Kolkata played all their home matches at Eden Gardens.[11]

Player retention

[edit | edit source]

Franchises were allowed to retain any number of players from their squad,[12] including traded players while excluding players signed as temporary replacements.[13] Franchises were required to submit their retention lists before 15 November 2025.[14] Kolkata retained twelve players, including captain Ajinkya Rahane.[15][16][17] Kolkata also traded Mayank Markande to Mumbai Indians.[18]

Auction

[edit | edit source]

The season's auction took place on 16 December 2025 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.[22] The auction purse for each franchise was set at ₹125 crore (US$13 million),[15] with franchises being deducted an amount from the purse for every retained player.[12][23] Kolkata had a purse remaining of ₹64.3 crore (US$6.9 million).[24] Kolkata bought thirteen players in the auction, including eight capped players and six overseas players.[25][26]

Support staff

[edit | edit source]

Abhishek Nayar replaced Chandrakant Pandit as the head coach[33][34] while Shane Watson replaced Ottis Gibson as an assistant coach[35] and Tim Southee replaced Bharat Arun and Carl Crowe as bowling coach.[36][37] Dishant Yagnik also joined the squad as a fielding coach.[38]

League stage

[edit | edit source]

Kolkata Knight Riders began their season with two losses to Mumbai[40] and Sunrisers Hyderabad.[41] Their third match against Punjab Kings was abandoned due to rain.[42] They lost their next three matches to Lucknow Super Giants,[43] Chennai Super Kings[44] and Gujarat Titans.[45] This was the first time Kolkata did not win any of their opening matches in a season.[46] The won their next four matches against Rajasthan Royals,[47] Lucknow,[48] Hyderabad[49] and Delhi Capitals;[50] lost to Royal Challengers Bengaluru[51] and won against Gujarat[52] and Mumbai.[53] They lost their last game of the season to Delhi[54] to finish the league stage at the seventh place with thirteen points and were eliminated.[55]
